evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/compliance/hooks/useAmlDashboard.ts:103 — the AML dashboard data transform calls `a.risk_factors.map((f) => ...)` with NO null/undefined guard, while the two sibling array transforms in the same function defensively guard their source with `?? []`: :96 `(assessmentsData?.assessments ?? []).map(...)` and :130 `(countryRisksData?.countries ?? []).map(...)`. The inconsistency means the author knows API collection fields can be absent at runtime, yet the nested per-assessment `risk_factors` array is dereferenced unguarded. The generated client type declares it non-optional (frontend/packages/api-client/src/compliance/types.ts:111 `risk_factors: AmlRiskFactor[];`), so TypeScript will NOT flag a missing-field case — but a real API/proxy response that omits the field or sends `risk_factors: null` for any single assessment throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'map')`. This transform runs synchronously in the hook body (not inside the TanStack queryFn and not inside any try/catch), so the throw surfaces as a React render crash of the whole AmlDashboardPage, not as a recoverable query `error` state. Severity MEDIUM (+2): crash path on a user-facing compliance screen, triggered by a single malformed row. Confidence MEDIUM: statically certain the guard is missing; not upgraded to high because it depends on the backend actually emitting a null/absent `risk_factors`. Fix: `(a.risk_factors ?? []).map(...)`. frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/compliance/hooks/useAmlDashboard.ts:112-117 — the per-assessment transform hard-codes five compliance-critical fields to falsy constants on EVERY assessment regardless of backend state: `id_verified: false`, `source_of_funds_documented: false`, `pep_check_completed: false`, `sanctions_check_completed: false`, `recommendations: []`. The AML risk dashboard therefore always renders every subject as PEP-check-not-completed, sanctions-check-not-completed and ID-not-verified. On a regulated AML/KYC surface this is a data-integrity/accuracy problem: a compliance officer reading the dashboard cannot distinguish 'check genuinely outstanding' from 'UI cannot yet show the result', which can drive wrong remediation decisions or mask completed screening. It is acknowledged as a phased gap by the inline `// TODO(Phase-2): Extend API to include these fields` / `// Phase 1: Default values for missing fields` at :110-111, so it is a known/tracked limitation rather than an accidental bug. Severity LOW (+1): no crash or auth impact, documented, but user-facing inaccurate compliance status. Confidence MEDIUM. Fix path: surface these fields from the AML assessment API (TypeSpec contract + generated client) and map real values, or render them as an explicit 'not available yet' state instead of a definitive `false`. Cloud-landable (ppt-web React SPA, frontend.yml CI verifiable); the API-extension portion is reality-independent on the frontend side but ultimately needs the backend field to carry real data.
